items.title: Hank Cicalo interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 30, 2022
items.q: Most of the producers I ever worked with, Tom Mack, at Capitol, and at RCA... I worked with Tom Mack, we worked with somebody in the big bands, he was in Glenn Miller’s original band. He was a producer at Dot Records. And you know he was just great to work with.

ctx.x: Did you work with producers that tended to over-hype the artist, like give them pep talks: “You’re going to be great, this is going to be terrific”?

A few. Most of the producers I ever worked with, Tom Mack, at Capitol, and at RCA, those guys would let you set it up. And as long as the artist was comfortable, and that’s the way I always felt — I put the rug down, put a couple of flats behind them, if they © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

wanted the room a little darker, if they didn’t want to face the control room, I always tried to work with them. If you get the artist comfortable and relaxed it’s 90 percent of the battle, you know? I hated to take more time, I’d start a date and then they’d tell the — make the changes, do this, do that, do that. And it would always interfere with what the vocalist was doing or the performer was doing. My thing was always to make them comfortable.
